To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
we have developed a direct-contact manganese-silicide p/n multilayers thermoelectric power generating block.
a direct contact multilayer thermoelectric device was fabricated using MnSi1.7 and Mn0.8Fe0.3 Si1.68 powders, and that it generated power of 11.7mW/cm2 at 700°C.
a maximum power output of about 11.7mW/cm2 was obtained at a temperature difference of 20°C and at 700°C, with a TE block consisting of 4 pairs of p/n MnSi layers.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the development of a direct-contact multilayer thermoelectric power generator.
the development of a direct-contact manganese silicide thermoelectric power generator.
the fabrication of multilayer-type TE devices using manganese silicide powders with low thermoelectric performance and the development of TE devices with high power density and high durability.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
this research has successfully fabricated multilayer direct contact TE blocks with a maximum output power of 11.7 μW/cm2 at 700°C.
this research has successfully developed a manganese silicide-based multilayer direct contact thermoelectric device with an output of 11.7mW/cm2.
the fabrication of a multilayer direct contact TE device using a screen printing process was successful, but the power generation efficiency is still too low to be used practically.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the multilayer direct contact TE device has a great potential to generate electric power from heat.
the maximum power generation of 1.3 mW/cm2 was achieved at a temperature difference of 200°C, which was 1/100 of the ideal power.
the multilayer TE device was fabricated by the doctor-blade method, hot pressing and spark plasma, and the output was measured by the hot plate method and engine test bench.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the power generation of a TE device can be enhanced by the number of TE p/n pairs.
the power generation efficiency of a multilayer-type TE device is significantly improved by increasing the number of TE p/n pairs.
the fabrication of a multilayer TE block using MnSi and Mn0.6Fe0.4Si materials is a promising method for improving TE power generation efficiency.
